'''John Pancras Mukasa Lubowa Ssebuwufu''', commonly known as '''John Ssebuwufu''' is a [[Uganda]]n [[chemist]], [[Academic staff|academic]] and [[Academic administration|administrator]]. He is a former [[chancellor (education)|chancellor]] of [[Kyambogo University]], Uganda's second-largest public university serving between 2014-2022 having served for 2 terms.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=Twinamatsiko |title=Prof. Okedi replaces Ssebuwufu as Kyambogo University Chancellor |url=https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/education/prof-okedi-replaces-ssebuwufu-as-kyambogo-uni-134093 |website=The NewVision |date=17 May 2022 |publisher=David Lumu |access-date=17 May 2022}}</ref> He was installed as chancellor on 19 February 2014, replacing Eric Tiyo Adriko, who had completed his two term tenure.<ref name="New">{{cite web|newspaper=[[New Vision]] (Kampala)|
url=http://www.newvision.co.ug/news/652742-prof-ssebuwufu-installed-as-kyambogo-chancellor.html|title=Professor Ssebuwufu Installed As Kyambogo Chancellor|date=19 February 2014|accessdate=29 January 2015 |first=Innocent|last=Anguyo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| 
url=http://www.monitor.co.ug/News/National/Tear-gas-welcomes-chancellor-Ssebuwufu-to-Kyambogo/-/688334/2213764/-/atwt9bz/-/index.html|title=Tear Gas Welcomes Chancellor Ssebuwufu To Kyambogo University|date=20 February 2014|accessdate=29 January 2015|last=Ssenkabirwa|
first=Al-Mahdi|newspaper=[[The Observer (Uganda)]]}}</ref> The correct spelling of his last name is ''Ssebuwufu''. However the literature contains many instances where the name is spelled with a single "s".

==Background==
He was born in Uganda's [[Central Region, Uganda|Central Region]] in 1947.

==Education==
Ssebuwufu attended [[Namilyango College]] for his middle and high school education in the 1960s. He studied at [[Makerere University]], for his [[Bachelor of Science]] and [[Master of Science]] degrees, both in [[Chemistry]]. In 1974, he won a scholarship to study for a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] at [[Queen's University Belfast]] in [[Northern Ireland]], from which he graduated in 1977. Ssebuwufu spent another two years at Queen's University on a postdoctoral fellowship also in chemistry.<ref name="New"/>

==Work experience==
On returning to [[Uganda]] in 1979, Ssebuwufu was appointed as [[lecturer]] in the Department of Chemistry at [[Makerere University]]. He continued in that position until 1985, when he was promoted to senior lecturer. In 1987, he became the head of the Chemistry Department at the university.

In 1990, he was elevated to the rank of [[professor]] and was appointed [[Principal (academia)|principal]] of the Institute of Teacher Education; now part of [[Kyambogo University]]. He served in that capacity until 1993 when he was appointed [[vice chancellor]] of [[Makerere University]], Uganda's oldest and largest public university. He served as vice chancellor until the expiration of his tenure in 2004.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=30 July 2014|url=http://vc.mak.ac.ug/about/history.html|title=Chronological List of Makerere University Principals And Vice Chancellors 1970 - 2012|publisher=[[Makerere University]], Office of the Vice Chancellor|date=2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140702050507/http://vc.mak.ac.ug/about/history.html|archive-date=2 July 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In February 2014, the [[President of Uganda]] appointed him chancellor of [[Kyambogo University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.observer.ug/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=30682:-ssebuwufu-to-resolve-kyambogo-problems|title=Ssebuwufu To Resolve Kyambogo Problems|date=16 March 2014|accessdate=30 July 2014|last=Nakabugo|first=Zurah|newspaper=[[The Observer (Uganda)]]|archive-date=8 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808060432/http://www.observer.ug/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=30682:-ssebuwufu-to-resolve-kyambogo-problems|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Other responsibilities==
In addition to his responsibilities at Kyambogo University, Ssebuwufu is the current Vice Chancellor of the University of Kisubi (UniK) which was formerly known as ''Kisubi Brothers University College'' (KBUC), a constituent college of [[Uganda Martyrs University]] to which he had also served as the Principal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kbuc.ac.ug/prof-john-sebuwufu/|title=Professor John Ssebuwufu: Principal of Kisubi Brothers University College|accessdate=30 July 2014|publisher=kbuc.ac.ug|archive-date=30 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140830225555/http://kbuc.ac.ug/prof-john-sebuwufu/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2013, he was appointed as the [[chairperson]] of the [[UbuntuNet Alliance]], the regional research and education network for [[Eastern Africa|Eastern]] and [[Southern Africa]]. In the past, he has served as the director of research programs at the [[Association of African Universities]] (AAU) in [[Ghana]].

Ssebuwufu is a member of the [[World Bank Millennium Science Initiative]] and is one of the technical experts for Uganda. He serves as the chairman of the [[board of directors]] for following Ugandan companies and businesses:

* [[Citibank Uganda]] - A subsidiary of [[Citigroup]] of [[New York City]]
* [[Uganda Management Institute]] (UMI)
* National Environment Management Authority of Uganda (NEMA)
* National Council for Science and Technology
